zfv42n.q: When a driver shows signs of tiredness, it is advisable to reach the nearest rest area and rest.
zfv42n.why: Tiredness reduces attention and reflexes. The only real remedy is to stop safely in a lay-by (piazzola di sosta) and rest.

1q8tzm9.q: When a driver shows signs of tiredness, it is advisable to get as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.
1q8tzm9.why: Getting closer cuts the safety distance, and a tired driver reacts slowly, so a rear-end crash becomes more likely. The right action is to stop and rest.

q6t016.q: Some hours must pass before a driver who has drunk an excessive amount of alcohol recovers fitness to drive.
q6t016.why: The body eliminates alcohol only with time, usually several hours. No quick fix restores fitness to drive.

178i8ad.q: A driver who has drunk an excessive amount of alcohol cannot quickly recover fitness to drive, especially if medicines were also taken.
178i8ad.why: Clearing alcohol takes hours, and medicines can strengthen its effects, so recovery is even slower.

1mb51k5.q: A driver who has drunk an excessive amount of alcohol can quickly recover fitness to drive by eating fairly salty foods.
1mb51k5.why: Salty food does not lower blood alcohol. Only time lets the body eliminate alcohol and recover fitness to drive.

1djpdef.q: A driver who has drunk an excessive amount of alcohol can quickly recover fitness to drive by drinking black coffee.
1djpdef.why: Coffee may make you feel more awake but does not lower blood alcohol. Only time eliminates alcohol.

ryn4r4.q: Fitness to drive can be impaired by the use of certain sedative medicines.
ryn4r4.why: Sedatives cause drowsiness and slow reflexes, so they can impair driving.

2f55q1.q: Fitness to drive can be impaired by the use of antidepressant medicines.
2f55q1.why: Antidepressants can cause drowsiness, reduced attention and slower reflexes, which can impair driving.

15efitt.q: Fitness to drive can be impaired by the use of hallucinogens (LSD, ecstasy, etc.).
15efitt.why: Hallucinogens distort perception and judgement and seriously impair the ability to drive.

zym1u3.q: Fitness to drive can be impaired by the use of alcoholic drinks.
zym1u3.why: Alcohol slows reflexes, reduces concentration and makes you underestimate danger, so it impairs driving.

10h9x66.q: Fitness to drive can be impaired by the use of black coffee.
10h9x66.why: Black coffee does not impair fitness to drive. It is a stimulant, not a substance that reduces driving ability.

levzdj.q: Fitness to drive can be impaired by the use of fizzy drinks.
levzdj.why: Fizzy drinks do not affect the mental and physical abilities needed for driving.

4ty4a3.q: Fitness to drive can be impaired by the use of mineral salt supplements.
4ty4a3.why: Mineral salt supplements do not alter mental or physical abilities and do not impair driving.

3pr4ty.q: Fitness to drive can be impaired by the use of dietary supplements.
3pr4ty.why: Dietary supplements are not among the substances that impair driving, unlike alcohol, drugs and certain medicines.

6utfa6.q: Taking hashish or marijuana can impair the ability to drive.
6utfa6.why: Cannabis alters perception, attention and reaction time, so it impairs driving.

zvqbfo.q: Taking heroin or cocaine can impair the ability to drive.
zvqbfo.why: Heroin and cocaine alter mental and physical condition and seriously impair driving ability.

1h0coor.q: Sedative medicines contain some substances that can impair the ability to drive.
1h0coor.why: Sedatives contain active ingredients that cause drowsiness and slow reflexes, so they can impair driving.

k6ibl6.q: Taking LSD or amphetamines does not impair the ability to drive.
k6ibl6.why: LSD and amphetamines alter perception, attention and judgement, so they always impair driving ability.

dq95yf.q: Taking hashish or marijuana does not impair the ability to drive.
dq95yf.why: Hashish and marijuana alter attention and reaction time, so they do impair driving ability.

1kp5haz.q: A heavy, excessive meal is not recommended for someone who has to drive.
1kp5haz.why: A heavy meal slows digestion, causes drowsiness and reduces attention, so eating light before driving is better.

1pv0aas.q: Eating foods that are hard to digest can reduce attention and increase reaction times.
1pv0aas.why: Hard digestion causes drowsiness and drops in attention, which lengthens reaction times.

e3wr8g.q: Drinking spirits (strong alcoholic drinks) during a large meal does not impair the ability to drive.
e3wr8g.why: Food does not cancel the effects of spirits. Alcohol still impairs driving, even during a large meal.

njh4xv.q: Alcohol can cause a state of euphoria, leading to underestimating danger.
njh4xv.why: Alcohol causes euphoria and false confidence, so the driver underestimates hazards.

y5hgln.q: Anyone driving while drunk (under the influence of alcohol) risks arrest.
y5hgln.why: Above 0.8 g/l blood alcohol, drink driving (guida in stato di ebbrezza) is a criminal offence and can lead to arrest.

14vz4xx.q: It is inadvisable to drive when in an altered emotional state.
14vz4xx.why: Anger, agitation or heavy stress reduce attention and self-control, so driving is inadvisable.

e1x0fo.q: Anyone driving a vehicle without a motor with a blood alcohol concentration above the legal limit is not subject to any penalty.
e1x0fo.why: The drink-driving rules also apply to vehicles without an engine, such as bicycles, so a penalty does apply.

1spvsjv.q: Anyone driving while drunk has faster reaction times.
1spvsjv.why: Alcohol slows reflexes and lengthens reaction times; it never speeds them up.

1s9pwv5.q: Helping an injured person on the road is required by law.
1s9pwv5.why: The Highway Code requires you to help an injured road user, and failing to do so is punished.

1dizdri.q: Helping an injured person on the road can mean saving their life.
1dizdri.why: Prompt help, even simple help, can be decisive for the injured person's survival.

19awgq0.q: Helping an injured person on the road immediately can prevent further physical harm.
19awgq0.why: Quick and correct help limits the worsening of injuries while waiting for the emergency services.

rfdpgh.q: Helping an injured person on the road is not a legal obligation, only a moral duty.
rfdpgh.why: Giving help is a legal obligation, not just a moral duty, and failing to do so is punished.

fqrxhs.q: You must help an injured person on the road only if you consider the accident serious.
fqrxhs.why: The duty to help always applies, whatever you think of the accident's severity.

ppx6ji.q: It is not mandatory to help an injured person on the road, so as not to endanger your own safety.
ppx6ji.why: The duty to help remains. You help as far as you can, at least by calling the emergency services, without taking needless risks.

1natvfd.q: Helping an injured person on the road is mandatory only for doctors and healthcare staff.
1natvfd.why: The duty to help applies to all road users involved or present, not only to medical staff.

1hp0ki.q: It is not mandatory to help an injured person on the road if doing so obstructs traffic.
1hp0ki.why: The duty to help takes priority over obstructing traffic, which is no excuse for not helping.

1i1ryu2.q: The aim of first aid is to try to keep the injured person alive through simple, immediate actions.
1i1ryu2.why: First aid aims to keep the injured person alive with simple, immediate actions, without replacing doctors.

vm7ztr.q: The aim of first aid is to assist the injured person as best as possible while waiting for medical help to arrive.
vm7ztr.why: First aid means assisting the injured person as well as possible until medical help arrives.

9grp73.q: During first aid, you must avoid, as far as possible, further harm to the injured person.
9grp73.why: Whoever helps must avoid, as far as possible, making the injured person's condition worse.

5qigpn.q: During first aid operations, you must avoid wrong or harmful actions being performed on the injured person.
5qigpn.why: Wrong actions can worsen injuries, so only simple, correct measures should be taken.

urevs9.q: The aim of first aid is to immediately ask the injured person how the accident happened.
urevs9.why: First aid is about keeping the injured person alive and assisting them, not questioning them about how the accident happened.

sgimd0.q: During first aid, the injured person must in every case be moved away from where they are.
sgimd0.why: The injured person must not be moved unless there is immediate danger, such as fire, because moving can worsen injuries.

fexefs.q: During first aid, you must never touch the injured person until the police have arrived.
fexefs.why: You do not wait for the police. You act immediately with the necessary first-aid measures.

11pwyk2.q: If an injured road user has a bleeding wound, it must be covered with sterile or as clean as possible material to stop the bleeding.
11pwyk2.why: A bleeding wound is covered with sterile or the cleanest available material to stop the bleeding and limit infection.

1po5ohf.q: If an injured road user has a bleeding wound dirty with soil, it must be washed as soon as possible with clean water.
1po5ohf.why: A wound dirty with soil should be washed as soon as possible with clean water to remove dirt and reduce infection risk.

13zn3x7.q: During first aid, if the injured person has a bleeding wound with foreign bodies embedded in it, they must not be removed from the wound.
13zn3x7.why: Embedded objects must not be removed, because they may plug the damaged vessel and removing them worsens the bleeding.

1gaxcfo.q: If an injured road user has a bleeding wound, it must be pressed with sterile gauze or clean cloths.
1gaxcfo.why: Press on the wound with sterile gauze or clean cloths to stop the bleeding.

16tc7bm.q: During first aid, if the injured person has a bleeding wound, any foreign bodies in it must be removed immediately and the wound covered afterwards.
16tc7bm.why: Embedded objects must never be removed. Cover the wound around them, since removing them increases bleeding.

1mvoqwb.q: If an injured road user has a bleeding wound and is unconscious, you must give them water or tea to drink.
1mvoqwb.why: Never give drinks to an unconscious person: they may choke and the liquid can worsen their condition.

1kdxr7u.q: If an injured road user has a bleeding wound, it must not be covered, to help the blood stop by itself.
1kdxr7u.why: The wound must be covered with clean or sterile material and pressed to stop the blood and protect against infection.

tdd9w3.q: If an injured road user has a bleeding wound, hot water must be poured on it to stop the bleeding.
tdd9w3.why: Hot water does not stop bleeding. The wound is pressed with clean or sterile material.

19tew49.q: If an injured road user has heavy external bleeding, you must press the wound and call for help immediately.
19tew49.why: Heavy bleeding is serious: press the wound at once and call the emergency services.

1no4m1y.q: If an injured road user has heavy external bleeding, the wound must be pressed immediately, applying pressure with clean or, if possible, sterile material.
1no4m1y.why: Press the wound immediately with clean or, if possible, sterile material to stop the blood loss.

bz0t89.q: If an injured road user has heavy external bleeding, you must try to stop the blood flow.
bz0t89.why: With heavy bleeding the priority is to stop the blood flow by pressing on the wound.

1cb6ykg.q: If an injured road user has heavy external bleeding, it is advisable, if possible, to place them in a seated or lying position while waiting for help.
1cb6ykg.why: A seated or lying position reduces the risk of fainting or falling while waiting for help.

7fz9ns.q: If an injured road user has heavy external bleeding, you must only dress the wound.
7fz9ns.why: Dressing is not enough: you must stop the bleeding by pressure and call the emergency services at once.

1q34fnx.q: If an injured road user has heavy external bleeding, you must cover the wound and make the injured person walk.
1q34fnx.why: Walking increases bleeding and the risk of shock. The injured person should stay still, seated or lying down.

8apveo.q: If an injured road user has heavy external bleeding, it is absolutely forbidden to give them water to drink.
8apveo.why: The ban on drinking is not absolute for a conscious casualty. Drinks are avoided mainly if the person is unconscious or internal injuries are suspected.

1pfbhc3.q: If a foreign body (glass splinter, wood or other) has got into an injured road user's eye, the eye must be bandaged, without any other manoeuvres.
1pfbhc3.why: Bandage the eye without trying to remove the foreign body, and wait for a specialist.

4wl5q4.q: If a foreign body has got into an injured road user's eye, they must be advised not to touch the damaged eye, to avoid further damage.
4wl5q4.why: Touching the eye can worsen the injury, so the casualty is told not to touch it.

1lhc6pb.q: If a foreign body has got into an injured road user's eye, it must be bandaged, avoiding touching it until a specialist intervenes.
1lhc6pb.why: The eye is bandaged and left untouched until a specialist treats it, to avoid more damage.

1rs0pnh.q: If a foreign body has got into an injured road user's eye, you must always try to remove it.
1rs0pnh.why: Never try to remove the foreign body. Bandage the eye and wait for a specialist.

sb9vzt.q: If a foreign body has got into an injured road user's eye, you must force them to keep their eyes open, to avoid other injuries.
sb9vzt.why: Forcing the eye open worsens the injury. The eye should be bandaged and kept closed.

esepzk.q: If a foreign body has got into an injured road user's eye, you must gently massage the eyelid, to encourage tears.
esepzk.why: Massaging the eyelid can move the object and worsen the damage. The eye should only be bandaged.

1l4jpd8.q: If a foreign body has got into an injured road user's eye, the injured eye must never be bandaged.
1l4jpd8.why: The injured eye should be bandaged, with no other manoeuvres, until a specialist arrives.

b32y9p.q: Shock shows itself with very pale, cold skin.
b32y9p.why: In shock, circulation drops and the skin becomes very pale and cold.

7f15m7.q: Shock shows itself with cold sweat on the forehead.
7f15m7.why: Cold sweating, especially on the forehead, is a typical symptom of shock.

53vhw2.q: Shock shows itself with shivering, very pale skin and cold sweating on the forehead.
53vhw2.why: Shivering, very pale skin and cold sweat on the forehead are typical shock symptoms.

1hlccj8.q: Shock shows itself with very pale skin, cold sweating and a rapid heartbeat.
1hlccj8.why: Pallor, cold sweating and a rapid heartbeat are typical shock symptoms.

1rec9kb.q: Shock can show itself with the sudden utterance of meaningless phrases and words.
1rec9kb.why: Shock can cause mental confusion, with meaningless words and phrases.

haj7yn.q: Shock always shows itself with a sharp rise in body temperature.
haj7yn.why: In shock the skin is cold and pale, and body temperature tends to fall, not rise.

10lah6b.q: Shock shows itself with large dark patches on the skin.
10lah6b.why: Shock shows as pallor and cold sweat, not dark patches on the skin.

xdsdda.q: Shock appears with red skin and strong hot flushes
xdsdda.why: In shock the skin is pale, cold and sweaty, not red and hot, and the pulse is weak and rapid.

iypm42.q: An injured person in shock must be laid on the ground and, if possible, with the legs raised
iypm42.why: A person in shock is laid down with the legs raised so blood flows to the brain and heart.

1gwvgha.q: An injured person in shock must be covered as well as possible to prevent them from getting cold
1gwvgha.why: In shock body temperature drops, so the person is covered to keep them warm.

khz11v.q: An injured person in shock must be laid down, keeping the legs raised if possible
khz11v.why: The correct position is lying down with the legs raised, which supports circulation to the vital organs.

19s6c5c.q: When there is an injured person in shock, they must be made to walk to restart their blood circulation
19s6c5c.why: A person in shock must not walk, as effort makes things worse. Keep them lying down and at rest.

1xf2utz.q: An injured person in shock must be put in a sitting position
1xf2utz.why: Sitting reduces blood flow to the brain. A person in shock should lie down with the legs raised.

jhw6re.q: When there is an injured person in shock, small slaps must be given on the cheeks and legs to restart their blood circulation
jhw6re.why: Slapping does not help and can make things worse. The person should be kept still, lying down and covered.

11xmfcv.q: When there is an injured person in shock, they must be given small amounts of spirits to drink
11xmfcv.why: A person in shock must not be given anything to drink, least of all alcohol, which widens blood vessels and worsens circulation.

1vv6r1d.q: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must check whether they are still breathing by placing a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the abdomen
1vv6r1d.why: Breathing is checked by feeling chest or abdomen movement, with a hand on the lower side of the chest.

1sti7zm.q: If a road casualty is unconscious, they may be moved only if you are sure they have no spinal injuries
1sti7zm.why: Moving a casualty can worsen a spinal injury, so it is done only when you are sure there is none.

act874.q: If a road casualty is unconscious and has difficulty breathing, you must immediately clear the nose and mouth of any obstructions
act874.why: If breathing is difficult, the priority is to clear the airway (vie aeree) of any foreign objects or secretions right away.

m11ehv.q: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must check their condition often until the ambulance arrives
m11ehv.why: An unconscious person's condition can change quickly, so breathing and consciousness must be checked continuously until help arrives.

vdvyco.q: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must give them alcoholic drinks
vdvyco.why: An unconscious person must never be given drinks: they could choke, and alcohol is harmful anyway.

1hm701o.q: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must hold their hands down
1hm701o.why: There is no need to restrain an unconscious person's hands. Check breathing and consciousness and avoid unnecessary movement.

gxpyst.q: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must bandage their head
gxpyst.why: Bandaging the head is not a first aid step for an unconscious person. It is done only to stop bleeding.

1op0bzd.q: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must put them in a half-seated position
1op0bzd.why: A half-seated position can block the airway. An unconscious person who is breathing goes in the recovery position (posizione laterale di sicurezza), if there is no spinal injury.

1en3bxi.q: If a conscious road casualty has suffered chest trauma, you must try to make breathing easier by placing them half-seated
1en3bxi.why: With chest trauma, a half-seated position makes breathing easier.

1r7ts6o.q: If a conscious road casualty has suffered chest trauma with a visible deep wound, you must immediately press on it with a clean cloth
1r7ts6o.why: A deep chest wound is pressed at once with a clean cloth to limit bleeding.

1x4qr4x.q: If a road casualty has suffered chest trauma, you must assist them until medical help arrives
1x4qr4x.why: The casualty must be assisted and reassured, and monitored, until medical help arrives.

1r1ycbw.q: If a road casualty has suffered chest trauma, you must make them take deep breaths
1r1ycbw.why: Deep breaths increase pain and can worsen chest injuries. Put the person half-seated and let them breathe normally.

sfkmri.q: If a road casualty has suffered chest trauma, you must lay them down with the legs raised
sfkmri.why: With chest trauma, lying with legs raised makes breathing harder. The half-seated position is used.

1v1zvpg.q: If a road casualty has suffered chest trauma, you must keep them standing to reduce blood loss
1v1zvpg.why: Keeping the person standing does not reduce blood loss and risks a fall. Seat them half-upright and press on any wounds.

3xxwpw.q: If a road casualty has suffered fractures to the limbs, the fractured limbs must not be moved
3xxwpw.why: Moving a fractured limb increases pain and damage, so it must be kept still.

1m04pz1.q: If a road casualty has suffered fractures to the limbs, you must immobilise them without carrying out other manoeuvres
1m04pz1.why: Fractured limbs are immobilised without other manoeuvres: do not move them or try to set the fracture.

1a0t0zw.q: If a road casualty has suffered fractures to the limbs, you must cover any wounds with clean material
1a0t0zw.why: Any wounds are covered with clean material to prevent infection.

1vnmwy.q: If a road casualty has suffered fractures to the limbs, you must immobilise them and immediately afterwards, if necessary, apply the normal anti-shock measures
1vnmwy.why: After immobilising, if the person shows signs of shock, apply anti-shock measures: lying down, legs raised, covered.

9jpx1e.q: If a road casualty has suffered fractures to the limbs, you must try to make them walk to reduce the pain
9jpx1e.why: Walking on a fracture worsens the injury and pain. The casualty must stay still with the limbs immobilised.

bu2c66.q: If a road casualty has suffered fractures to the limbs, you must ask them to move them to assess the type of injury
bu2c66.why: Asking someone to move fractured limbs can worsen the injury. Assessing the injury is for medical staff.

7d2zhl.q: If a road casualty has suffered fractures to the limbs, with a bone protruding, you must try to push it back into the tissues
7d2zhl.why: A protruding bone must never be pushed back. Cover the wound with clean material and wait for the rescuers.

4i9ba8.q: If a road casualty has suffered fractures to the limbs, you must give them a spirit drink
4i9ba8.why: Casualties must not be given drinks, least of all spirits, which harm circulation and may complicate treatment.

ffxqei.q: If a road casualty has been burned and flames are still present, you must put them out by smothering them, for example with a blanket
ffxqei.why: Remaining flames are smothered, for example with a blanket, to stop the burning.

1wbe2fm.q: If a road casualty has been burned, it is advisable not to remove clothes stuck to the burned skin
1wbe2fm.why: Clothes stuck to burned skin are left in place, because pulling them off would tear the skin and worsen the injury.

1mosn4w.q: To reduce the pain of burns, cold water should be used if possible
1mosn4w.why: Cold water cools the burned area and eases the pain.

1nmwth6.q: If a road casualty has burns on the trunk, it is best to cover them with clean material, preferably sterile
1nmwth6.why: Burns are covered with clean, preferably sterile material to protect them from infection.

iitwlc.q: If a road casualty has been burned and flames are still present, you must wait for them to go out on their own before intervening
iitwlc.why: Flames must be put out immediately, for example by smothering them with a blanket, not left to die out on their own.

270nj7.q: If a road casualty has been burned, you must always remove the parts of clothing that have stuck to the skin
270nj7.why: Clothing stuck to burned skin must never be removed, as this would worsen the injury.

10hy71j.q: If a road casualty has been burned, you must disinfect the burns with alcohol
10hy71j.why: Alcohol on a burn causes pain and damage. Cool it with cold water and cover it with clean material.

y887b1.q: After a road accident, the rescuer who intervenes must assess the situation carefully in order to protect the injured from further dangers
y887b1.why: The rescuer first assesses the scene to protect the injured from further dangers such as passing vehicles or fire.

1icvyy0.q: After a road accident, the rescuer who intervenes must assist the injured as best they can, without however taking initiatives that are the specific responsibility of medical staff
1icvyy0.why: The rescuer helps as best they can but does not do things reserved for medical staff, such as giving medication.

12ieepl.q: After a road accident, the rescuer who intervenes must assist the injured according to their own abilities and knowledge
12ieepl.why: The rescuer helps within their own abilities and knowledge, without attempting what they cannot do.

up2x2l.q: Anyone involved in a road accident must always and immediately leave the place where it happened
up2x2l.why: Anyone involved in an accident must stop and help, not leave. Fleeing the scene is penalised.

1brht9r.q: In the event of a road accident, you must only wait for rescuers to arrive, without doing anything
1brht9r.why: Those able to must act: secure the scene, call for help and assist the injured as far as they can.

1p4f86f.q: In the event of a road accident, the first thing the rescuer must do is identify the injured person by asking for their first and last name
1p4f86f.why: The first step is to assess the scene, make it safe and call for help, not to ask for personal details.

1k8yjaz.q: In the event of a road accident, the rescuer must give medication to the victim if the rescuer has no specific medical competence
1k8yjaz.why: Giving medication is for medical professionals. Someone without medical training must not give any to the victim.

wjga2d.q: The state of shock can be caused by severe pain
wjga2d.why: Severe pain is one possible cause of shock, along with trauma, bleeding and intense emotion.

jbs660.q: The state of shock can be caused by a strong emotion (joy, anger)
jbs660.why: A strong emotion, whether joy or anger, can also cause shock.

18g8eq0.q: The state of shock can be caused by heavy blood loss
18g8eq0.why: Heavy blood loss reduces circulation and can cause shock.

i0noma.q: The state of shock can be caused by a severe trauma
i0noma.why: A severe trauma is a typical cause of shock.

1s917zj.q: The state of shock cannot depend on strong emotions
1s917zj.why: Strong emotions are among the possible causes of shock, along with pain, trauma and bleeding.

6wabzp.q: The state of shock never occurs in people who have suffered a trauma
6wabzp.why: Trauma is a typical cause of shock, so it can occur in people who have suffered one.

3iqbri.q: The state of shock never occurs in people who have lost a lot of blood
3iqbri.why: Heavy bleeding is a typical cause of shock.

10vooog.q: The state of shock does not represent a danger to health
10vooog.why: Shock is a serious condition that can be life-threatening if untreated.

1ufcmw9.q: Taking alcohol makes driving less safe, because it can cause excitement and recklessness
1ufcmw9.why: Alcohol can cause euphoria and recklessness, making driving less safe.

g18n85.q: Taking alcohol makes driving less safe, because it can slow down reflexes
g18n85.why: Alcohol slows reflexes and increases reaction time.

17yqj1.q: Taking alcohol makes driving less safe, because it can cause drowsiness
17yqj1.why: Alcohol can cause drowsiness, which is dangerous when driving.

1q10yo7.q: Taking alcohol makes driving less safe, because it can dangerously alter the ability to concentrate and pay attention
1q10yo7.why: Alcohol impairs concentration and attention, making driving dangerous.

i8k9ms.q: Taking alcohol can reduce the level of attention

101to7m.q: Taking alcohol makes driving safer, because it cancels out tiredness
101to7m.why: Alcohol does not remove tiredness: it masks it while lowering alertness and reflexes, making driving less safe.

qsz0bt.q: Taking alcohol makes driving easier, because it increases the ability to concentrate
qsz0bt.why: Alcohol reduces the ability to concentrate rather than increasing it, making driving less safe.

1hecndj.q: Taking alcohol makes driving easier, because it makes you more alert and attentive
1hecndj.why: Alcohol lowers alertness and attention; it only gives a false sense of confidence.

xuzpxf.q: Taking alcohol makes driving safer, more cheerful and less boring
xuzpxf.why: Alcohol makes driving more dangerous: it slows reflexes, reduces attention and encourages recklessness.

18s5gfi.why: Alcohol worsens vision: it narrows the field of view and impairs perception of lights and distances.

158e157.q: While driving, glasses or contact lenses must be worn if this obligation is shown on the licence
158e157.why: If the licence requires corrective lenses, the obligation applies while driving.

13j0j0v.q: While driving, glasses or contact lenses must be worn if the harmonised code "01" has been entered on the licence
13j0j0v.why: The harmonised code 01 means glasses or contact lenses are required while driving.

1mhxyk9.q: While driving, glasses or contact lenses must be worn if this obligation appears on the licence, in full or as a code
1mhxyk9.why: The obligation applies whether written out in full or shown as a code.

1gnopo2.q: While driving, glasses or contact lenses must be worn when this is indicated on the licence
1gnopo2.why: If the licence indicates it, wearing glasses or contact lenses while driving is mandatory.

10b2t1f.q: While driving, glasses or contact lenses must be worn only when short-sightedness exceeds 6 dioptres
10b2t1f.why: The obligation does not depend on a dioptre threshold but on the requirement shown on the licence.

oguxpj.q: While driving, glasses or contact lenses must be worn from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise
oguxpj.why: The obligation is not tied to the time of day: it always applies when it is shown on the licence.

1a422j.q: While driving, glasses or contact lenses must be worn only in conditions of poor visibility
1a422j.why: The obligation applies at all times while driving, if shown on the licence, not only in poor visibility.

16pqhvq.q: While driving, glasses or contact lenses must be worn only on motorways and main extra-urban roads
16pqhvq.why: The obligation applies on every road, if shown on the licence, not only on motorways and main extra-urban roads.
